title: A drop of everyday science
subject: Science
description: Explore how water changes, travels, and connects a village.
body: Water can be a solid, liquid, or gas. Ice is solid water. The water in a cup is liquid. Water vapour in the air is a gas.
Sunlight warms water in rivers and ponds. Some of it evaporates into the air. When the air cools, the vapour condenses into tiny droplets that make clouds.
Droplets join and become heavy. They fall as rain. Some rain flows into rivers; some soaks into the soil. This movement is called the water cycle.
Observe a cold cup on a warm day. Droplets on the outside came from water vapour in the air, not from water leaking through the cup.
question: What is the change from liquid water into water vapour called?
